# One-time migration baseline for the oasdiff breaking-change check.
#
# Each entry below is a `breaking change` that existed on the day we moved
# from the hand-curated `docs/openapi.yaml` to the generated version. Every
# one of them falls into one of three buckets:
#
#   1. The pre-migration spec was over-constrained (documented a shape the
#      runtime never actually enforced). Our Zod schemas now describe the
#      real runtime contract, which oasdiff flags as "breaking" because it
#      narrows the documented surface. Example: `scores.source` became an
#      enum; empty strings are now rejected where they weren't before —
#      but the runtime has always rejected them.
#
#   2. The pre-migration spec was under-constrained or outright wrong
#      (e.g. `span.timestamp` documented as `number` when runtime returns
#      an ISO string). Fixing that improves client accuracy.
#
#   3. Structural style differences between hand-curated prose and
#      chanfana output (e.g. empty `{}` schema -> `type: object`).
#
# These are NOT regressions consumers will hit at runtime. We pin them as
# accepted once; from the next PR forward, oasdiff compares against the
# newly-generated baseline and catches any REAL breaking changes.
#
# When adding new routes or changing existing ones, do NOT extend this file
# to paper over an accidental break — fix the underlying schema so oasdiff
# passes cleanly. A deliberate, documented product removal (a route or field
# nobody serves anymore, its callers updated in the same change) is the one
# legitimate reason to add an entry; every section below states which one
# it is and why.

# --- response body shape (hand-curated main had empty schemas) ---
in API GET /health the response's body type/format changed from ``/`` to `object`/`` for status `500`
in API GET /v1/annotation-queues the `data/items/` response's property type/format changed from ``/`` to `object`/`` for status `200`
in API GET /v1/health/files the response's body type/format changed from ``/`` to `object`/`` for status `200`
in API GET /v1/health/files the response's body type/format changed from ``/`` to `object`/`` for status `503`
in API GET /v1/health/ingestion the response's body type/format changed from ``/`` to `object`/`` for status `200`
in API GET /v1/health/ingestion the response's body type/format changed from ``/`` to `object`/`` for status `503`
in API GET /v1/templates the `data` response's property type/format changed from ``/`` to `object`/`` for status `200`

# --- stub routes (experiments, prompts return 501 on cloud; content stripped) ---
in API GET /v1/experiments removed the media type `application/json` for the response with the status `200`
in API GET /v1/experiments/{experimentId} removed the media type `application/json` for the response with the status `200`
in API GET /v1/prompts removed the media type `application/json` for the response with the status `200`

# --- scores: Zod now reflects actual runtime enforcement ---
in API GET /v1/scores the `query` request parameter `resource_type` was restricted to a list of enum values
in API GET /v1/scores the `query` request parameter `source` was restricted to a list of enum values
in API POST /v1/scores request property `source` was restricted to a list of enum values
in API POST /v1/scores the `name` request property's minLength was increased from `0` to `1`
in API POST /v1/scores the `resource_id` request property's minLength was increased from `0` to `1`
in API POST /v1/scores/batch request property `scores/items/source` was restricted to a list of enum values
in API POST /v1/scores/batch the request property `scores/items/resource_id` became required
in API POST /v1/scores/batch the `scores/items/name` request property's minLength was increased from `0` to `1`
in API POST /v1/scores/batch the `scores/items/resource_id` request property's minLength was increased from `0` to `1`

# --- spans: hand-curated types were wrong vs runtime ---
in API GET /v1/spans the `data/items/timestamp` response's property type/format changed from `number`/`` to `string`/`date-time` for status `200`
in API GET /v1/traces/{traceId}/spans/{spanId} the `data/output_object` response's property type/format changed from `object`/`` to `string`/`` for status `200`
in API GET /v1/traces/{traceId}/spans/{spanId} the `data/tool_calls` response's property type/format changed from `array`/`` to `string`/`` for status `200`

# --- datasetName format constraint ---
# Added z.string().min(1).regex(/^[\w./-]+$/) to the datasetName path param.
# Schemathesis found that garbage bytes (C1 control chars etc.) in the path
# reached Supabase, hit Wrangler's request timeout, and produced a 503.
# No real client sends control characters as a dataset name — the runtime
# was already rejecting these inputs (via a slow-path 503); this makes the
# rejection explicit, fast, and spec-accurate (400 with a clear message).
in API POST /v1/datasets/{datasetName}/rows for the `path` request parameter `datasetName`, the minLength was increased from `0` to `1`
in API POST /v1/datasets/{datasetName}/rows added the pattern `^[\w./-]+$` to the `path` request parameter `datasetName`

# --- hard removal: GET /v1/traces/export ---
# Endpoint was staging-only with no production callers — confirmed out of
# band with its author. Normally oasdiff requires a Deprecation +
# Sunset cycle before removal (and the other two consolidation targets,
# `/v1/traces/{traceId}/graph` and `/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/traces`,
# got that treatment). /v1/traces/export skipped the cycle
# because its format-transform wedge (jsonl/openai/csv) is thin enough
# that callers can replicate it in 3 lines against GET /v1/traces —
# keeping a deprecation shell around for 6 months carries no upside.
# This exception covers the one-time delete; future endpoint removals
# should follow the deprecate-then-remove pattern the other two used.
in API GET /v1/traces/export api path removed without deprecation

# --- /v1/datasets canonical envelope upgrade ---
# `GET /v1/datasets` was returning the legacy `{ datasets: string[] }` flat
# shape. The REST-API-parity pass collapsed that endpoint into the
# canonical `{ data: [{ name, row_count, created_at }], pagination }`
# envelope used by every other list endpoint, so the `datasets` property
# is gone from the response body. The CLI is the only known consumer and
# was updated with the same change; its version plan was bumped from minor
# to major to signal the break to anyone on an older CLI. Future list
# endpoints that need a shape change should follow the same pattern
# rather than a parallel `/list` path with deprecation headers.
in API GET /v1/datasets removed the required property `datasets` from the response with the `200` status

# --- score `source` enum: eval → experiment|annotation|api ---
# Deliberate, documented break (same pattern as the /v1/datasets entry above).
# The score Source enum was renamed: automated experiment evals are now
# `experiment` (was `eval`), human annotations stay `annotation`, and direct
# sdk.score()/REST submissions are `api`. The legacy `eval` value is no longer
# accepted on write or as an analytics filter (default is now `api`). Rows
# already stored as `eval` still DISPLAY in the dashboard; only the write/query
# API surface drops it. OSS api-schemas took a minor version bump with the same change.
in API POST /v1/scores removed the enum value `eval` of the request property `source`
in API POST /v1/scores/batch removed the enum value `eval` of the request property `scores/items/source`
in API GET /v1/scores removed the enum value `eval` from the `query` request parameter `source`

# --- retirement of the prompt-product API surface ---
# The prompt-monitoring product is retired; these path families were removed
# DELIBERATELY (product decision, not schema drift): alerts, annotation-queues,
# trace sessions, metrics, filter-schema, experiments, prompts, runs, templates.
# One literal line per retired operation (oasdiff ignore matches substrings,
# not regex) — an accidental removal of any KEPT route still fails the gate.
in API DELETE /v1/alerts/{alertId} api path removed without deprecation
in API DELETE /v1/annotation-queues/{queueId} api path removed without deprecation
in API DELETE /v1/annotation-queues/{queueId}/items/{itemId} api path removed without deprecation

in API GET /v1/alerts/{alertId} api path removed without deprecation

in API GET /v1/metrics api path removed without deprecation

# The git-push→build→deploy pipeline, cloud datasets, score-configs, and the
# env promote/rollback saga are retired DELIBERATELY (a product decision).
# Their tables/functions are dropped in the
# same PR, so a deprecation cycle would stub endpoints that cannot work; the

# literal line per removed operation/property — an accidental removal of any
# KEPT route still fails the gate.

# --- GitLab provider removal: new connects are GitHub-only; the runtime returns a structured 409 for legacy gitlab rows ---
in API POST /v1/apps/{appId}/git/connect removed the enum value `gitlab` of the request property `provider`

# --- /health reports a count instead of naming unset variables ---
# The route is `security: []` — unauthenticated by design, because a probe has
# to reach it, so its body carries no configuration detail. `missing` and
# `configure_at` are replaced by a `missing_count`; the names go to the logs,
# where the operator who needs them already looks. Nothing but tests read this
# body, and it is only ever returned alongside a 500.
in API GET /health removed the required property `missing` from the response with the `500` status
in API GET /health removed the required property `configure_at` from the response with the `500` status

# --- environments drop `machine_status` ---
# The field reported whether an environment had a live runtime machine. Nothing
# has produced one since the runtime was retired, so it answered 'none' for
# every environment on every call. The column it derived from is dropped in the
# same change.
in API GET /v1/environments removed the required property `data/items/machine_status` from the response with the `200` status
in API POST /v1/environments removed the required property `data/machine_status` from the response with the `201` status
in API GET /v1/environments/{id} removed the required property `data/machine_status` from the response with the `200` status

# --- OTLP vendor-ingest subsystem retirement (2026-08-04) ---
# The OTLP prompt-monitoring surface is retired: the trace-ingest routes had
# no deployed consumers left once the OTLP normalizers, the dataset/
# experiment/prompt read stack, and the Cloudflare Queues ingest consumer
# were removed together. `prompt_name` is dropped from the span
# read routes because it was only ever populated from that stack.
in API GET /v1/spans removed the required property `data/items/prompt_name` from the response with the `200` status
in API POST /v1/spans/search removed the required property `data/items/prompt_name` from the response with the `200` status
in API GET /v1/spans/{spanId} removed the required property `data/prompt_name` from the response with the `200` status
in API GET /v1/traces api path removed without deprecation
in API POST /v1/traces api path removed without deprecation
in API POST /v1/traces/search api path removed without deprecation
in API GET /v1/traces/{traceId} api path removed without deprecation
in API GET /v1/traces/{traceId}/spans api path removed without deprecation
in API GET /v1/traces/{traceId}/spans/{spanId} api path removed without deprecation
